claims.text: AI-credited flaws reach CISA's exploited list no more often than other flaws.
By the end of 2028, AI-powered malware is used in a ransomware attack on UK critical national infrastructure, as the UK government or the NCSC publicly confirms.
The flood of new flaws is lasting, not a passing wave: at the end of 2028 the 13-week count of new CVE records is still at least 300% above (4 times) its 2023 to 2024 average (+432.6% on 8 Nov 2026).
AI flaw-finding keeps scaling beyond Anthropic: at the end of 2027 the 13-week count of AI-credited flaws excluding Anthropic is at least 450 (224 in the 13 weeks to 8 Nov 2026).
Exploitation speeds up: at the end of 2027 the whole 80% range of the 26-week median days from disclosure to CISA's exploited list is under 15 days (13 to 22 on 8 Nov 2026; 2023 to 2024: 15 to 36).
AI agents prove hard to control: by the end of 2028 an authority in the US, UK, EU, Japan or Taiwan reports a new case of an AI agent causing a breach without its owner's consent.
Unpatched holes get exploited more: Verizon's 2028 Data Breach Investigations Report puts exploited vulnerabilities above 31% of breaches with a known way in (2026 report: 31%).

Geopolitics turns AI flaw-finding into a state weapon: by the end of 2028 the US, UK, Japan, Taiwan, the EU or an EU state blames a foreign state for a new intrusion using AI to find or exploit flaws.
